title: Last iterates and ambiguous extrapolation
subtitle: Finite-step Muon · Rashomon fits · IV prediction · Lottery Ticket
intro: Two main readings and nine briefs, including one version watch: update geometry near zero and divergent extrapolations with nearly equal fitting loss. The classic separates sparse structure, initialization, and discovery cost.

articles.paper: Ambiguous Fits: The Rashomon Effect and Challenges in Scaling Law Estimation
articles.title: Equal fit quality need not mean equal forecasts
articles.evidence: Read Sections 2–4, Algorithm 1 and limitations; code not run

blocks.text: Chinchilla (2022) fitting commonly uses multi-start local optimization. This paper separates global optimization accuracy from agreement among nearly optimal extrapolations.[2]

blocks.tex: L(x;\vartheta)=E+\sum_{i=1}^k A_ix_i^{-\alpha_i},\qquad R(\vartheta)=\sum_n h_\delta\!\left(\log L(x_n;\vartheta)-\log y_n\right)
blocks.label: x denotes resource axes, y observed loss; h_delta is Huber loss with threshold delta [2]
Notation for explanation: Theta is a declared compact domain; the envelope covers predictions of near-optimal fits [2]

blocks.text: A monotone reparameterization bounds residuals over parameter boxes. Branch-and-bound splits promising boxes and discards those whose lower bounds cannot beat the incumbent. Stopping certifies its gap to a global lower bound. Four real scaling ladders demonstrate divergent extrapolation with nearly equal fit error.[2]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The envelope describes optimization ambiguity for fixed data, model family and parameter domain. It is not a confidence interval for future observations and does not cover training randomness or model misspecification.[2]

classic.paper: The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis: Finding Sparse, Trainable Neural Networks
classic.title: Sparse structure is not enough: which initialization survives?
classic.evidence: Read Sections 1–4, experimental setup and reinitialization controls; an empirical hypothesis, not a general existence theorem
classic.question: Replacing SGD by Muon, do initialization sensitivity and mask transferability change separately?

blocks.text: Pruning (LeCun et al., 1990; Han et al., 2015) showed that trained networks can be compressed. The lottery hypothesis asks whether the subnetwork trains independently from its original initialization. Let d count parameters and m be a fixed binary mask.[12,13]

blocks.label: Weights outside the mask remain zero [12]

blocks.tex: \exists m:\quad \|m\|_0\ll d,\qquad j_m\le j_{\rm dense},\qquad a_m\ge a_{\rm dense}
blocks.label: Original hypothesis: j is the minimum-validation-loss iteration and a its test accuracy [12]
Algorithm restatement: train, magnitude-prune, reset each round; trained values are not retained [12]
Key control fixes the mask and resamples initialization, separating structure from initialization [12]

blocks.text: MNIST fully connected and CIFAR10 convolutional experiments support the hypothesis. Original initialization generally beats reinitializing the same mask. Deep networks are learning-rate sensitive: VGG-19 at 0.1 did not yield winning tickets without warmup, but did with it. Iteration savings exclude repeated mask discovery.[12]
